newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares fall in kerb deals on Congress news.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares fall in kerb deals on Congress news.

text.p: Indian shares fell sharply in off-market kerb deals across the country on Sunday as speculators sold on news that the Congress Party had withdrawn support to the ruling coalition and staked a claim to form the government, brokers said.
In Bombay, shares of Reliance Industries -- India's largest private firm -- plunged 11 rupees, or 3.8 percent, to 274.
Reliance was trading 20 rupees, or 6.8 percent lower at 274 in Calcutta and 16.75 rupees, or 5.8 percent, down in Delhi.
Leading commercial bank State Bank of India (SBI) dropped to 290 rupees from its last official close of 303 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday.
SBI shares were trading 22.50 rupees lower at 290 in Calcutta and 18.10 rupees lower at 285 in Delhi.
"Volumes are low in Calcutta as most brokers had squared up their positions in A group stocks ahead of those shares going online on April 4," said a broker at Lohia Securities in Calcutta.
Traders said panicky speculators were cutting long positions as they expected markets to fall sharply on Monday.

"Panic has set in due to the fears that the coalition government of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda might collapse following withdrawal of support by the Congress party," said Manoj Choraria of brokers Choraria Associates.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority United Front alliance controls some 178 deputies in the 545-member Lok Sabha, or lower house. The Congress has 142 deputies.
Congress officials said the withdrawal decision followed "attempts by the United Front" to split the Congress party in the key northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
"Uncertainty over the budget which has yet to be passed mainly concerned the marketmen and triggered panic selling," said S.C Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit.

In the budget for 1997/98 (April-March), Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced sweeping cuts in corporate and personal taxes. Parliament had been expected to pass the proposed budget after reconvening in the second half of April.
